theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is a guest "folio"?
options: The guest's passport and visa papers
The record of a guest's charges and payments
A list of the rooms free to sell tonight
The menu card placed in each guest room

questions.stem: When is a guest's account normally opened?
options: When the guest pays the final bill
When the guest first orders room service
On the guest's second night at the villa
At check-in, when the guest registers

questions.stem: What does "posting" a charge mean?
options: Adding the charge to the right guest's account
Mailing the bill to the guest's home address
Putting the menu prices up on the staff notice board
Paying the supplier for the guest's tour

options: The waiter's name and the time of their shift
The colour of the slip and the size of the tip
The guest's name and room number on the slip
The price of the drink at other bars in town

options: So the bill is correct if the guest checks out early
So that the guest is charged interest on each charge
So that the supervisor has less work in the morning
So that the charge slip can be thrown away at once

questions.stem: Why does the guest sign a charge slip for a meal?

To give the waiter permission to leave
To book the same table for tomorrow

questions.stem: After a charge slip has been posted, what should you do with it?
options: Throw it away, as the charge is now on the system
Keep it with the day's records for checking
Give it back to the waiter to use again
Post it a second time to be sure it went in

questions.stem: You posted a J$4,500 dinner to the wrong guest's account. What should you do?
options: Delete the entry and say nothing to anyone
Leave it, as the guest may not notice
Correct it with an adjustment, and record why
Ask the guest to pay it and claim it back later

questions.stem: A guest was charged for a minibar drink they did not take. Who must approve taking the charge off the account?
options: The guest staying in the next room
Any staff member who is free
The housekeeper who checked the minibar
A supervisor or manager

questions.stem: A guest asks the villa to pay a taxi driver J$3,000 for them and add it to their account. What is this called?

A deposit
An allowance
A discount

questions.stem: When you make a paid-out for a guest, what must you get?

A receipt from the driver and the guest's signature
Permission from the taxi driver's boss
A tip from the guest for doing the job

questions.stem: A guest paid a deposit when booking. Where does it appear on the account?
options: As a charge, which makes the bill higher
It does not appear, as it was paid before
As a payment (credit), which lowers the balance
Only on the bank statement the guest gets at home

questions.stem: A guest's account shows charges of J$38,000 and payments of J$25,000. What is the balance owing?
An account shows charges of US$420 and a deposit of US$500. What is the balance?
options: The guest owes US$80 more
The guest owes US$920 in all

A US$80 credit to the guest

questions.stem: A guest pays US$100 towards their account. The villa's rate for the day is US$1 = J$155 (a made-up rate for this question only). How much is that in J$?
Which exchange rate must be used when a guest pays in US$ towards a J$ account?
options: The rate printed in yesterday's newspaper
The rate the property sets for that day
The rate that the guest says is fair
Any rate that makes the sum easy to work out

questions.stem: GCT must be added to a charge. Which rate do you use?
options: Whatever rate the guest asks for
A rate you remember from last year
No rate, as tourists never pay GCT
The current rate, set by law

questions.stem: What is a "credit limit" on a guest account?
options: The most a guest may owe before being asked to pay
The lowest price that a guest can be charged for a room
The most nights a guest is allowed to stay at the villa
The number of credit cards a guest can own

questions.stem: A guest's balance has gone over the credit limit. What should you do?
options: Lock the guest out of the room at once
Ignore it until the day the guest leaves
Tell your supervisor, as the policy says
Tell the other guests that this guest owes money

questions.stem: At check-in, the villa takes a "pre-authorisation" on the guest's card. What does this do?
options: It takes full payment for the whole stay at once
It holds an amount on the card to cover the charges
It checks the guest's age and home address
It cancels the card so that it cannot be used

options: Write the full card number in the front desk diary
Keep photocopies of the cards in an open drawer
Never write down full numbers or security codes
Read the card number aloud to check it with the guest

questions.stem: A company has agreed to pay for its staff member's room. Where is the room charge sent?
options: To the company's account, as agreed
To the staff member's personal bank
To the villa owner's own account
To the guest's home address by post

questions.stem: The company pays for the room only. The guest pays for meals and drinks. How is this set up?
options: One account, paid by whoever checks out first
All charges go to the guest, who claims them back
All charges go to the company, who claims them back
Two folios: room to the company, extras to guest

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the night audit?
options: To clean the front desk at the end of each day
To check all postings and balance the day's accounts
To count the guests who are asleep in their rooms
To lock the safe deposit boxes for the night

questions.stem: During the night audit, which charge is usually posted to every occupied room?
options: The minibar charge
The room charge for the night
The laundry charge
The airport transfer fee

questions.stem: A caller says she is Mrs Brown and asks for her account balance. What should you do first?
options: Read out the balance and the list of charges
Give the balance only, without the details
Refuse to speak to her at all and hang up the phone
Check that she is the guest, as the policy says

questions.stem: A guest at the desk asks for a printed copy of their account. What should you check?
options: That they have eaten in the restaurant today
That the account has a balance over J$10,000
That they are the registered guest
That they paid cash for their deposit

options: You cannot share a guest's account details
Tell him the total, but not each drink

questions.stem: A guest says a lunch charge on their account is wrong. What is the best first step?
options: Tell the guest that the system is never wrong
Remove the charge at once without checking

Check the signed slip with the guest

questions.stem: A guest checked out an hour ago. A bar slip for them has just reached the desk. What is this called?
options: A late charge
A deposit
An allowance

options: Throw away the slip, as the guest has left

questions.stem: A guest pays J$20,000 in cash towards the account. What should you do?
options: Put the cash in your pocket until the shift ends

Count it later, when the desk is not so busy

questions.stem: A guest moves from Room 4 to Room 7 during the stay. What must happen to the account?
options: A new account is opened, and the old one is deleted
The guest pays the old balance and starts again
Nothing; the charges stay with Room 4

questions.stem: Two friends in different rooms agree that one will pay for both rooms. What should you do?
options: Move the charges without asking either guest
Ask each guest to pay half of the total
Get both to agree in writing, then transfer
Wait and see who comes to the desk first

questions.stem: Why should every posting and correction be recorded with the name of the person who made it?
options: So that every change can be checked later
So that the desk looks busy to the guests
So that staff do not have to use the system
So that charges can be changed without anyone knowing

questions.stem: What does a "high balance report" show?
options: Guests staying in the rooms on the top floor
Guests whose balance is near or over their limit
The rooms with the highest price per night
Staff who have sold the most extras this week

questions.stem: A villa adds a service charge to guests' accounts. When must the guest be told about it?
options: Before the service, at booking or check-in
Only after they have paid the whole final bill
Never, as it is only a small amount
Only if they ask about the charges

questions.stem: A guest says a staff member promised them a 20% discount. What should you do?
options: Give the discount, as the guest says it was promised
Refuse rudely, as discounts are never given
Ask the guest which staff member they liked best
Check with your supervisor first

questions.stem: You leave the front desk for a few minutes. What should you do with the accounts system?
options: Leave it open so the next person can use it
Turn the screen to face the guests in the lobby
Log off or lock the screen
Write your password on a note by the keyboard

questions.stem: Why must you never share your password for the accounts system?
options: It would make the computer run more slowly
Every posting is linked to the person who logged in
The guests might use it to book more rooms
A password wears out if many people use it

questions.stem: A guest staying for two weeks asks to see their charges so far. What should you do?
options: Tell them to wait until check-out day
Give them the account of another guest by mistake
Tell them the balance, but refuse a printout
Print or show the folio after checking it is them

questions.stem: What is the best way to check that you posted a charge correctly?
options: Ask the guest whether the amount looks about right
Check that the screen looks the same as yesterday
Compare the posting with the signed slip
Wait for the night audit to find any errors

questions.stem: On the evening before a guest leaves, why might the desk check the guest's account?
options: To find and fix any errors before check-out
To add extra charges the guest did not use
To decide which staff member gets the tips
To remove the room charge for the last night

questions.stem: A guest's card is declined when you try to take a payment. What should you do?
options: Tell everyone in the lobby that the card was refused
Tell the guest privately and ask for another payment
Cut up the card in front of the guest
Keep trying the card until it goes through

questions.stem: A walk-in guest wants to open an account and charge meals to the room. What should you check first?
options: Their favourite meal at the restaurant
The make of their car in the car park
Their photo ID and a way to pay, such as a card
Whether they have stayed at other villas

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What do the letters GCT stand for?

In front office, what is the name for a guest who leaves without paying their account?

essays.stem: Explain what a guest folio is, and describe what it shows.
essays.modelAnswer: A guest folio is the record of everything a guest is charged and everything they pay during their stay. It is opened at check-in, when the guest registers, and closed when the guest has paid at check-out. The top of the folio shows the guest's name, the room or villa, the arrival and departure dates, the room rate, the number of guests and how the guest will pay, such as a card, cash or a company. Below this, each charge is listed with the date, a short description such as "room", "dinner" or "laundry", the slip number and the amount, with tax at the current rate where it applies. Payments, deposits and allowances are shown as credits. The folio also shows the running balance, which is what the guest owes at that moment, and the currency, J$ or US$.
markingPoints: Record of all charges and payments for one guest's stay
Opened at check-in and closed when settled
Shows the guest's details, room, dates, rate and payment method
Each charge with date, description, slip number and amount (and tax)
Payments and allowances as credits, a running balance and the currency

essays.stem: Describe the steps for posting a charge from a restaurant charge slip to a guest's account, and how you check that it is correct.
essays.modelAnswer: When the slip arrives from the restaurant, I check that it shows the guest's name and room, the date, the items and the total, and that the guest has signed it. I check that the name and room on the slip match a guest who is staying, and that the account is allowed to take charges. I then open the right account, choose the right department code, such as restaurant, and type the amount and the slip number carefully, as soon as possible. Before saving, I compare the screen with the slip again, especially the room number and the amount, to avoid swapped digits. After posting, I write or stamp "posted" on the slip and keep it with the day's records. At the end of the shift, I add up the slips and check that the total matches the total posted, so that any mistake can be found and corrected.
markingPoints: Checks the slip is complete and signed
Matches the name and room to a guest who is staying
Posts promptly to the right account and department with the slip number
Checks the screen against the slip before saving; marks the slip posted and files it
Totals slips against postings at the end of the shift

essays.stem: Explain how to correct an error on a guest's account, and why corrections must be authorised and recorded.
essays.modelAnswer: If I find an error, such as a charge on the wrong room or a wrong amount, I do not delete it or change the slip. I tell my supervisor and follow the property's procedure. Usually, the wrong entry is reversed with a correction or allowance, and the right charge is then posted to the right account. The correction form or the system notes the date, the amount, the reason, the account numbers and my name, and the supervisor approves it with a signature or code. Corrections must be authorised and recorded because they change the money the property is owed. Without control, mistakes could be hidden or money could be stolen by changing accounts. A clear record lets the night auditor and the manager check every change, keeps the accounts honest, and helps answer any question the guest asks later.
markingPoints: Never delete entries or change slips
Tells the supervisor and follows the procedure
Reverses with a correction or allowance and posts the right charge correctly
Records date, amount, reason, accounts and name, with supervisor approval
Why: protects against hidden mistakes and theft, and lets every change be checked

essays.stem: Describe how to handle a paid-out for a guest, such as paying a taxi driver or a delivery on the guest's behalf.
essays.modelAnswer: First, I check that the property allows paid-outs for this guest, and that the amount is within the limit, asking my supervisor if it is large. I check the amount the supplier is asking for, in J$ or US$. I get the guest's agreement, and the guest signs a paid-out slip with the amount and the reason. I pay the supplier from the paid-out or petty cash float, counting the money carefully, and I get a receipt from them with the date, the amount and their name. I post the paid-out to the guest's account at once, with the slip number, and attach the receipt to the slip. The slip and receipt go with the day's records, so that the cashier and night auditor can check that the money paid out matches what was posted. Finally, I tell the guest that the charge has been added to their account.
markingPoints: Checks it is allowed and within the limit (supervisor for large sums)
Guest agrees and signs a paid-out slip
Pays the supplier carefully and gets a dated receipt
Posts it to the account at once with the slip number
Files slip and receipt for checking; tells the guest

essays.stem: Explain how credit limits on guest accounts are watched, and what should be done when a guest goes over their limit.
essays.modelAnswer: Each account has a credit limit, which is the most the guest may owe before they are asked to pay. It may be set by the property's policy, by the amount pre-authorised on the guest's card, or by an agreement with a company. Front office staff watch the balances as charges are posted, and the night audit prints a high balance report each day, listing the guests who are near or over their limit. When a guest goes over the limit, the staff member tells the supervisor and does not act alone. The supervisor may raise the card pre-authorisation with the guest's agreement, or ask the guest politely and privately for a payment towards the account. Staff never talk about it in front of other guests. Until it is sorted out, the supervisor may stop further charges to the room. Everything that is done is recorded.
markingPoints: Credit limit explained (policy, card pre-authorisation or company agreement)
Balances watched when posting, and the high balance report each day
Over the limit: tell the supervisor; do not act alone
Supervisor raises the pre-authorisation or asks politely and privately for payment
May stop further charges; recorded

essays.stem: Explain how you would take a payment in US$ towards a guest account that is kept in J$.
essays.modelAnswer: First, I find the property's exchange rate for that day from the office or the system, and I never use a rate of my own or one the guest suggests. I tell the guest the rate and work out the J$ value of the US$ they want to pay, using a calculator, and show them the sum. For example, if the rate given were US$1 = J$150 (a made-up rate), then US$200 would be J$30,000. If the guest pays in cash, I count the notes in front of them and check that they are real, as the property's procedure says. I post the payment to the account in J$, with a note of the US$ amount and the rate used. I give the guest a receipt showing the US$ received, the rate and the J$ credited, and the new balance. The cash goes into the cash drawer and is recorded for the end-of-shift count.
markingPoints: Uses only the property's rate for that day
Tells the guest the rate and works out the J$ value accurately
Counts cash in front of the guest and checks the notes
Posts the payment correctly with the US$ amount and rate noted
Gives a receipt with US$, rate, J$ and the new balance; cash recorded

essays.stem: Explain how front office staff protect the privacy and security of guests' accounts and card details.
essays.modelAnswer: A guest's account is private, so staff discuss it only with the guest, or with a person the guest has named in writing, such as the company that pays. Before giving a balance or a copy of the folio, staff check that they are talking to the registered guest, for example by asking for ID at the desk, or by following the policy for phone calls. Staff never read out balances or room numbers where others can hear, and never give account details to visitors or callers. Card details are handled carefully: the full card number and security code are never written down, cards are not photocopied unless the policy allows it, and the card stays in sight of the guest. The computer screen is locked or logged off when the desk is left, passwords are never shared, and printed folios are kept out of sight and shredded when no longer needed.
markingPoints: Discusses the account only with the guest or someone named in writing
Checks identity before giving balances or copies (ID; phone policy)
Never says balances or room numbers aloud, or tells callers or visitors
Card details protected: no full numbers or codes written; card kept in sight
Screen locked, passwords private, papers kept out of sight and shredded

essays.stem: Describe how a guest's account is opened at check-in, and what must be set up so that charges can be posted to it during the stay.
essays.modelAnswer: When the guest checks in, the front office agent finds the reservation and confirms the guest's name, dates, room and rate. The agent checks the guest's photo ID, and the guest signs the registration card. The account (folio) is then opened in the system or on a folio sheet and linked to the room, with the guest's name, the arrival and departure dates, the room rate, the meal plan and the currency the account is kept in. The agent asks how the guest will pay and sets this up: for a card, a pre-authorisation is taken to cover the expected charges; for cash, a deposit is taken and a receipt is given. Any deposit paid when booking is shown as a credit. The agent sets the credit limit and notes whether the guest may sign meals and drinks to the room. If a company pays part of the bill, split folios are opened. The agent checks every detail before saving.
markingPoints: Confirms the reservation, checks photo ID and has the registration card signed
Opens the folio linked to the room, with name, dates, rate, meal plan and currency
Sets up payment: card pre-authorisation, or cash deposit with a receipt
Shows any booking deposit as a credit; sets the credit limit and whether charges to the room are allowed
Opens split folios where a company pays part; checks the details before saving

essays.stem: Explain the difference between the guest ledger and the city ledger, and describe how a split folio works for a guest whose company pays part of the bill.
essays.modelAnswer: The guest ledger holds the accounts of guests who are staying in the property now. The city ledger holds accounts that will be paid after the guest has left, such as companies or travel agents that have an agreement to be billed, and guests who left without paying in full. When a guest checks out and the bill is to be sent to a company, the balance is moved from the guest ledger to the city ledger. A split folio is used when two people or bodies pay different parts of the bill. For example, a company agrees to pay for Mr Campbell's room and tax only. At check-in, two folios are opened: folio A for the room and tax, sent to the company's city ledger account at check-out, and folio B for meals, drinks, laundry and calls, which Mr Campbell pays himself before he leaves.
markingPoints: Guest ledger: accounts of guests staying now
City ledger: companies and agents billed later, and unpaid accounts of guests who have left
Balance moved to the city ledger at check-out when billed to a company
Split folio: two folios for two payers
Correct example: room and tax to the company; extras paid by the guest

essays.stem: Describe how you would deal with a guest who disagrees with a charge on their account.
essays.modelAnswer: I would listen politely to the guest without arguing, and thank them for raising it. I would check that I am speaking to the registered guest, and then go through the folio with them in private, away from other guests. I would find the signed charge slip, the date and the time, and look at it with the guest. If the slip shows the charge is correct, for example their signature is on it, I would explain this calmly and show them. If there is a mistake, such as a wrong room or wrong amount, I would say sorry and tell my supervisor, who approves a correction or allowance, and I would give the guest a new copy of the folio. If I cannot settle it, I would ask the supervisor to speak to the guest. I would record the query and what was done, and pass it on to the department concerned.
markingPoints: Listens politely without arguing; checks it is the guest; talks in private
Checks the signed slip and details with the guest
Explains calmly if correct
If wrong: apologises, supervisor approves a correction, new folio given
Refers to the supervisor if unsettled; records it and informs the department

practical1.title: Post a day's charges to guest folios and balance them
practical1.brief: Use the Centre's front office training software or paper folio sheets. The assessor gives the group made-up folios for five guests (each with a deposit or a card pre-authorisation and a credit limit) and a pack of made-up charge slips for one day: restaurant, bar, minibar, laundry and a tour, plus one paid-out with a receipt, one slip with the wrong room number, one minibar charge the guest disputes (with a supervisor-approved allowance form), and one payment in US$ with a made-up exchange rate the assessor gives. Each member is responsible for at least one folio. Check each slip, post it to the right folio, deal with the wrong-room slip and the allowance correctly, post the US$ payment at the given rate, and work out each balance. As a group, fill in a daily posting control sheet: the total of the slips must match the total posted. Each member explains one posting and one balance to the assessor. Photograph each stage below and add the photos, folios and control sheet to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: The Centre's front office training software, or paper folio sheets
Made-up guest folios and a pack of made-up charge slips, a paid-out slip with receipt and an allowance form (from the assessor)
A made-up exchange rate for the day (from the assessor)
A daily posting control sheet, a calculator and pens
A phone or tablet to take the photos
photos: The pack of slips sorted by guest before posting
Each member posting a slip, with the slip beside the folio or screen
The wrong-room slip and how it was dealt with
The allowance form signed by the "supervisor" and the folio after the correction
The US$ payment worked out and posted
Each completed folio showing the balance
The daily posting control sheet balanced
checklist: Checked each slip for name, room, date, amount and signature before posting
Posted each charge to the right folio and department, with the slip number
Found the wrong-room slip and posted it correctly
Applied the allowance only with the supervisor's approval, and recorded the reason
Worked out and posted the US$ payment correctly at the given rate
Helped balance the control sheet, finding and correcting any difference
Kept guest details private and slips in order
safety: Use only made-up guest names, card details and amounts
Sit correctly at the screen and take short breaks from it
Keep cables tidy and walkways clear
Shred or return all practice slips with guest details at the end

practical2.title: Credit check, account enquiries and a split folio (role play)
practical2.brief: Using the made-up folios from the assessor, the group first prepares a high balance report: list every guest whose balance is near or over their credit limit, and say what action is needed. Then set up a split folio for a made-up company guest whose company pays the room and tax only, and post a set of charges to the right folio. Next, each member in turn plays the front office agent in one role play with a "guest" or "caller" (another member or the assessor): a guest who asks for a copy of their account (check ID); a caller who says she is a guest and asks for her balance; a visitor who asks what another guest has spent; a guest who is over the credit limit (involve the "supervisor"); a guest who disputes a charge; and a guest who wants to pay part in J$ and part in US$ at the made-up rate the assessor gives. Each member records their role play in the front office log. Photograph each stage below and add the photos, report, folios and log to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Made-up guest folios with credit limits and a company agreement (from the assessor)
High balance report form, blank folio sheets (or training software) and a front office log
Made-up ID cards for the role plays and a made-up exchange rate (from the assessor)
A phone or tablet to take the photos
photos: The two split folios with charges posted correctly
An ID check at the desk, with the made-up ID
Each member's role play in progress
The receipt for the part-J$, part-US$ payment
The front office log with every enquiry recorded
checklist: Listed every guest near or over the limit and gave a suitable action
Set up the split folio correctly and posted each charge to the right folio
Checked identity before giving any account information
Refused politely to give account details to a visitor or an unchecked caller
Referred the over-limit guest to the supervisor and spoke to the guest privately
Handled the disputed charge calmly, using the signed slip
Worked out the mixed J$ and US$ payment correctly and gave a correct receipt
Recorded the enquiry clearly in the log
safety: Use only made-up guest names, ID and card details
Speak about account details quietly, as you would at a real desk
Keep the desk area clear and cables tidy
Shred or return all practice papers with guest details at the end
